research_question: Can the exact x86_64 Sandlock asset, exact Tycho source and patch, licenses, and credential-free isolation probe be assembled into a compact deterministic offline input bundle suitable for a later internet-disabled target-kernel preflight?

parent_evidence.established: Sandlock v0.8.6 and the exact Tycho patch passed filesystem, network, process, timeout, memory, and unit checks on one pinned Ubuntu 26.04/aarch64 VM.
parent_evidence.unresolved: The target evaluator kernel and x86_64 asset have not executed.

bundle_contract.format: deterministic ZIP with fixed timestamps, sorted paths, and normalized modes
required_payload: original Tycho source archive and exact patch

pass_criteria.input_hashes: Every frozen source, release, patch, and license hash matches before packaging.
pass_criteria.patch: The exact R1 patch applies cleanly to the exact Tycho source archive before the runtime package is copied.
pass_criteria.architecture: Static ELF inspection identifies the packaged Sandlock executable as x86-64 Linux.
pass_criteria.determinism: The builder emits a sorted relative manifest and fixed-metadata ZIP whose bytes are independently verified.
pass_criteria.size: The ZIP is no more than 20,000,000 bytes.
pass_criteria.runner: Static verification confirms fail-closed feature checking, protected-root denial, reachable TCP/UDP controls, child-process denial, timeout and memory probes, and no host fallback.

claim_boundary.supports_if_pass: Only that the exact target-preflight inputs can be assembled reproducibly into a compact offline x86_64 bundle.
does_not_support: model loading, inference, GPU fit, or throughput

stopping_rule: Stop after one bundle build, one independent manifest verification, and one static ELF inspection. Do not upload, run the target notebook, execute x86_64 Sandlock, use credentials, load a model, access ARC, run OIA, or submit.
